title: Definite assignment and strictPropertyInitialization
hook: strictPropertyInitialization ensures class fields are assigned before use — either in the declaration, constructor, or via definite assignment assertion. It mirrors C# rules about reading uninitialized fields, but only at compile time.

blocks.text: **Definite assignment analysis** tracks whether variables and class properties are assigned before read. **`strictPropertyInitialization`** (part of strict) errors when a class field lacks initializer and is not set in every constructor path. **`strictNullChecks`** enables the analysis for `undefined` reads. The **definite assignment assertion** (`name!: string`) tells the compiler an external initializer will run — common in Angular `@Input()` patterns. Like all TS checks, this is **compile-time only** — uninitialized fields are still `undefined` at runtime if you lie to the compiler.

entries.plainDefinition: Requires class properties be initialized in declaration or constructor.
Property postfix !: field will be assigned before use outside constructor.
Control-flow tracking of whether variables are assigned on all paths.
entries.example: let x: string; if (ok) x = 'a'; console.log(x); // error

blocks.text: Uninitialized class fields caused silent `undefined` bugs before strictPropertyInitialization. Frameworks that set fields after construction (Angular, NestJS DI) need `!` or optional types. C# also forbids reading unassigned locals and warns on nullable fields — similar intent, CLR still allows reflection to see default values.

blocks.title: Prefer initialization over !
blocks.body: Default values in declaration or constructor assignment beat definite assignment assertion when possible.

blocks.text: strictPropertyInitialization does not analyze methods called from constructor unless this is fully assigned first. Parameter properties (constructor(private x: string)) satisfy initialization. Abstract classes: subclasses must initialize abstract-implied fields. Migration: enable strict, fix fields batch by batch. C# required modifier (C# 11) parallels non-optional required init.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected
blocks.body: Disabling strictPropertyInitialization instead of fixing fields. Thinking ! initializes at runtime. Not knowing parameter properties satisfy the checker.

interviewTakeaways: strictPropertyInitialization: class fields must be set in declaration or constructor.
name!: T is compile-time only — framework must actually assign.
Definite assignment analysis applies to locals on all code paths.
60s: strict ensures fields initialized. Use ctor, inline default, or ! for DI/framework. C# similar for locals. Runtime still undefined if wrong.
commonPitfalls: Weak: ! initializes the field — it only silences the compiler.
Weak: disabling strictPropertyInitialization globally — fix initialization instead.
Strong: Inline init or constructor assignment first. ! only for proven framework lifecycle. Optional ? when truly optional.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS class fields default to undefined silently — TypeScript strict catches missing initialization at compile time.
constructor(private x: string) declares and assigns in one line — satisfies strictPropertyInitialization.
